pr_title: [WIP] Add GpuMatND with arbitrary dimension support
pr_body:
### Pull Request Readiness Checklist

See details at https://github.com/opencv/opencv/wiki/How_to_contribute#making-a-good-pull-request

- [x] I agree to contribute to the project under OpenCV (BSD) License.
- [x] To the best of my knowledge, the proposed patch is not based on a code under GPL or other license that is incompatible with OpenCV
- [x] The PR is proposed to proper branch
- [x] There is reference to original bug report and related work
- [ ] There is accuracy test, performance test and test data in opencv_extra repository, if applicable
      Patch to opencv_extra has the same branch name.
- [ ] The feature is well documented and sample code can be built with the project CMake

This PR aims to add support for arbitrary dimension support as a first step to support the APIs given in https://github.com/opencv/opencv/issues/16433
As of creating this PR only interface is added and comments on the same is awaited.

```
force_builders_only=docs,Custom
buildworker:Custom=linux-4
build_image:Custom=ubuntu-cuda:16.04
```
pr_comments:
> There should be interoperability with 2D `GpuMat`

I will try to keep this in mind while implementing the interface.
@YashasSamaga @alalek Please let me know if any change is to be made in the interface.
I hope I can start working on the implementation now. As no more comments are received on the interface. Probably we can minor changes during writing the implementation. Thanks.

> I think it is better to have a C++11 interface (what's the point of having C++98 interface when OpenCV has already moved to C++11).

Actually, I am not aware about which parts of the interface of `GpuMat` that are there due to C++98. For example, there is something called `Allocator`. Why don't we use `static` methods to reserve space in the memory and call them in the initializer list of constructor? Please let me know if we can do this and which functions can we remove from `GpuMatND`.

Hi,
Any thoughts on the ideas given in https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/16666#issuecomment-595111320 or can I proceed with the current interface given in the diff?
Please let me know.
Thanks.
Is anyone still working on this?

Bumping. Is there any chance of this being completed soon? I think `GpuMat` is currently the only way to pass GPU memory to `InputArray`/`OutputArray`. This is very limiting. And not all GPU data are 2D images.

There are frameworks that are benchmarking DNN performance by measuring inference time on GPU. All OpenCV DNN CUDA related benchmarks include D2H and H2D transfer which makes comparisons across frameworks unfair (and the data transfer cost isn't even negligible sometimes). And this extra data transfer cost also hurts OpenCV DNN's CUDA backend benchmarks where other frameworks do full preprocessing and postprocessing on GPU.

Hi, 

First of all apologies for not responding. It's been a long time since I updated this PR. If anyone's interested, please feel free to take this over and complete it. 

Apologies again. Stay safe.

##### Detailed description

To my knowledge, OpenCV still has no implementation for GpuMats with more than 2 dimensions.
This has been a feature of `cv::Mat` for a long time, but for some reason it has never been applied to `GpuMat`, which creates a disconnect when transferring algorithms from CPU implementations to GPU implementations.

This is an example of a `cv::Mat` function that creates a multi-dimensional matrix:
https://docs.opencv.org/master/d3/d63/classcv_1_1Mat.html#a156df5a1326dd5c30b187b0e721a5f57
